title: About Typeface
markdown:
For AI agents: the docs index is at https://typeface.readme.io/llms.txt. Append .md to any documentation page URL to get its markdown version.

Typeface is a platform where your team's agents create content. You describe what you need, agents produce it under your brand rather than a generic one, and the results land on a canvas you can review, arrange, and send onward.

* * *

### The four things you work with   [Skip link to The four things you work with](https://developers.typeface.ai/docs/introduction\#the-four-things-you-work-with)

| **Workspace** | **Document** | **Profile** | **Agent** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Where a body of work lives. A project workspace holds a single effort; a library workspace holds the shared material that every project draws on. | One produced thing, and it knows what kind of thing it is - an email, a banner ad, a landing page, a video script. Its type decides how it renders and where it can go. | Your brand is captured as something agents can read: tone of voice, visual style, the target audience, and the approved assets to draw from. | Does the work in steps, choosing tools as it goes. You can use the supplied agents or build your own, and run them on demand or on a schedule. |

> 📘
>
> **Workspace** and **Profile** are the everyday names for ideas covered in full on [Conceptual Data Model](https://developers.typeface.ai/docs/introduction-conceptual-data-model): a Workspace is a Team's Projects (project workspace) plus its shared, organisation-wide resources (library workspace); a Profile is your Brand Kit and Audiences together. Reach for that page when you need the precise terms.

* * *

### What a document can be   [Skip link to What a document can be](https://developers.typeface.ai/docs/introduction\#what-a-document-can-be)

A document is typed, and the type is doing real work: it determines the editor you get, the layout rules applied, and which channels the result can be delivered to.

| **Family** | **Includes** | **Typically ends up** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Campaign** | Email, push notification, in-app message | In your marketing or messaging platform |
| **Advertising** | Banner ad, ad variations | In an ad platform, sized per placement |
| **Web** | Landing page, reusable page module | In your CMS |
| **Visual** | Image, graphic | In your asset library, or inside another document |
| **Video** | Script, short-form cut, export | Downloaded or handed to an editor |
| **Written** | Document, structured markdown | Shared as-is, or as a source for the above |

* * *

### How a piece of work actually goes   [Skip link to How a piece of work actually goes](https://developers.typeface.ai/docs/introduction\#how-a-piece-of-work-actually-goes)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| You describe it | In plain language, in a chat or a form. No prompt engineering required — the brand context is already attached. |
| The agent works | It plans, reads your profiles and connected content, calls the tools it needs, and produces output as it goes rather than in one shot. |
| Results appear on the canvas | Each output becomes a node you can move, group and compare side by side. Variations sit next to each other rather than replace one another. |
| **You react** | Comment, edit directly, or ask for another pass. Feedback re-enters the same run rather than starting over. |
| It leaves Typeface | Published through a connector to the system that owns that channel, pushed to your endpoint, or pulled by your own code. |

> 📘
>
> **Why the canvas, and not a list of files**. Content work is comparative — you judge three subject lines against each other, or one ad across five sizes. A canvas keeps every candidate visible at once, with its history and comments attached, so choosing is a matter of looking rather than opening things one at a time.
